what_it_does: Designing computer chips (RTL—register-transfer level, the standard blueprint language for modern chips) requires engineers to make early choices about power consumption, speed, and size. Normally, these trade-offs are locked in early; if the final chip doesn't meet goals after manufacturing simulation (synthesis), the design must be redone. This paper proposes using a large language model combined with reinforcement learning (a machine learning technique that learns through trial-and-error reward) to write RTL descriptions that are better aligned with target power, performance, and area goals. The LLM receives real synthesis metrics as feedback during code generation, steering it toward better designs instead of requiring manual iteration.
